card.name: History and citation context endings
card.fires_on: Words in historical or archaeological passages and old-book citations, such as the end of a site name, a book title, or a period phrase like 'years before Columbus'. It fires on the word just before the text could continue with a past-era detail.

modes.label: Historical prose
modes.description: Nouns or word parts in text about ancient or past events and archaeology.
modes.example: Intriguingly, the prehistoric<< site>> of Göbekli Tepe sits right

modes.label: Citation endings
modes.description: Periods or publisher words closing a reference to an older book.
modes.example: The Journals of Captain James Cook<<.>> Cambridge: Cambridge University Press.

modes.label: Past-time phrases
modes.description: Words in phrases placing something in the past, such as years before an event.
modes.example: the Chinese visited America more than 70<< years>> before Columbus.

card.writes: It suppresses history-related words like historian and historical, and promotes words like recent and currently, so it pushes toward present-time wording over historical wording.
card.plain: It lights up in history and old-book reference text, and it nudges the model away from history words.
